description_en: This riverside rest house (sataḥ) situated on the banks of the Bagmati river at Gaurīghāṭa primarily serves as a venue for conductingśrāddharituals, which are periodic ceremonies dedicated to ancestral worship.This east-facingsataḥis a two-story edifice with a corrugated metal sheet roofing on the gable. The upper floor is adorned with an intricately carved three-bayed latticed window at its center, flanked by a smaller latticed window on each side. The central window is notably unique for featuring carvings of mother goddesses and intricate arches. The ground floor of thesataḥis divided into five bays in the eastern wing, with the western wing featuring a central entrance leading to an enclosed room. Additionally, on the southern side of thesataḥ, one can find embedded statues of Śiva, Viṣṇu, and Gaṇeśa on the wall.While the construction of thesataḥis attributed to an army officer named Jayanta Kumedāna, the exact year of its establishment remains unclear. An inscription on the northern wall of thesataḥcommemorates the construction of a cremation ground (ghāṭa) in front of thesataḥby Śivānanda Vaidya in 1826 CE (NS 946) and credits Jayanta Kumedāna with the construction of thesataḥ. However, an inventory published by the Kathmandu Upatyakā Nagara Vikāsa Yojanā mistakenly indicates that Jayanta Kumedāna built thesataḥin 1826 CE, the same year the cremation ground was established. In 1967 CE (VS 2024), thesataḥunderwent renovation, with the upper floor being repurposed for accommodation (Inventory VS 2039, p.88). As of September 2023, an ascetic has taken residence on the upper floor.Thesataḥis utilized for conductingśrāddharituals, which involve the periodic veneration of deceased family members. In the past, during the occasion ofṚṣiPañcamī, which falls on the 5th of the bright fortnight of Bhādra, women used to perform a holy bath in the Bagmati river and employed thesataḥfor changing and warming themselves by a fire (local resident, Ācārya, male, age 59). However, this tradition of bathing in the river is no longer practiced.
description_ne: गौरीघाटको नदि तटमा बनेको यो सतः मिल्दो परम्परागत अनुपातका कारण आकर्षक छ । घाटमा बनेको सतः मूलतः श्राद्ध संस्कार गरिँदा सुविधा होस भन्ने हेतु बनेको हो र यही प्रयोजनका लागि प्रयोग हुँदै आएको छ ।वागमती नदि किनारमा पूर्वतिर फर्काई सतः बानाइएको छ । पूर्वाभिमुख सतःको भूमि तलामा पाँच कवलको फल्चा निकालिएको छ । सतः दुई नाले भएकाले भूमितलामा फल्चा हुँदै प्रवेश गर्न सकिने कक्ष छ । माथिल्लो तलामा आकर्षक सँझ्याः हालिएको छ । मातृकाका मूर्ति र तोरण चढाइएका कमैमात्र सँझ्याः उपत्यकामा पाइन्छन् जसमध्ये यो पनि पर्दछ । सँझ्याःको दायाँ-बायाँ दुई तिकिझ्याः हालिएका छन् । परम्परागत पेगोडा शैलीमा बनेको दुईपाखे छानो जस्तापाताले छाइएको छ ।पशुपति क्षेत्रमा बनेका प्राय सम्पदाहरू राज्यमा पदस्थ पात्रहरूबाट बनेका पाउँछौं । यो सतः पनि जयन्त कुमेदान नामक सेनामा पदस्थ पात्रले बनाएक जुन । 'कुमेदान' तत्कालीन सेना संगठनको एक उच्चपद जनाउने शब्द हो (हेर्नुहोस् Glossary) । सतःको बायाँतिरको पर्खालमा नेसं ९४६ (सन् १८२६) को एक शिलात्र छ । उपत्यका नगर विकास योजनाद्वारा विसं २०३९ (सन् १९८२) मा प्रकाशित एकइन्भेनटोरीमा गल्तीवस् यसै अभिलेखलाई आधार मानी जयन्त कुमेदानले नेसं ९४६ (सन् १८२६) मा सतः बनाएको भनी उल्लेख परेको छ (Inventory VS 2039, p.88) । वास्तवमा यो अभिलेखमा शिवानन्द वैद्यले यस सतःको अग्र भागमा घाट बनाई राखेका हुन् तर यस अभिलेखमा यस सतःका निर्माता भनी जयन्त कुमेदानको नामोल्लेख गरिएको छ । शिवानन्दले घाटका साथै माधवनारायणको मूर्ति स्थापना गरी विविध ठाउँमा जग्गा गुठी राखेका थिए । विसं २०२४  (सन् १९६७) मा सतःको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको हो र यस ताका  माथिल्लो तला स्थयी निवासका खातिर प्रयोग गरिएको थियो (Inventory VS 2039, p.88) । हाल (अगष्ट २०२३) सतःमा एक सन्यासी बाबाजि बस्दै आएका छन् ।सतः गौरीघाटमा हुने श्राद्ध कार्यलाई लक्षित गरी बनाइएको देखिन्छ । विगत ऋषि पञ्चमीमा वागमती किनारमा रातको समय नुहाउनेको भीड लाग्ने गर्दथ्यो र यो सतःको फल्चालाई लुगा फेर्ने र आगो ताप्ने ठाउँको रूपमा प्रयोग गर्ने गरिन्थ्यो  (local resident, Ācārya, male, age 59) । यी थिति लोप भैसकेको अवस्था छ । सतःबाट दक्षिणतिरको गारोमा लहरै शिव, विष्णु, गणेश आदि मूर्तिहरू राखिएका छन् ।

historical_events.event_description: An inscription on the northern wall of thesataḥcredits Jayanta Kumedāna with the construction of thesataḥwhile documenting the construction of a cremation ground (ghāṭa) by Śivānanda Vaidya in the front. However, an inventory published by the Kathmandu Upatyakā Nagara Vikāsa Yojanā mistakenly indicates that Jayanta Kumedāna built thesataḥin 1826 CE, the same year the cremation ground was established. Śivānanda also established a statue of Mādhavanārāyaṇa in the vicinity and set up a trust by donating land.

An inventory published by the Kathmandu Upatyakā Nagara Vikāsa Yojanā mentions that thesataḥunderwent renovation in 1967 CE (VS 2024). However, it does not specify the agent that carried it out nor clarifies the nature of the renovation.
